investigator.method: Level 1 PASSIVE_STATIC only: curl (plain HTTP GET, descriptive User-Agent 'BandOnTheMap-SourceInvestigation/0.1 (+https://github.com/chriswatson6675/band_on_the_map)', no authentication, no browser/JS execution) against the venue's own official 'Programme' page. Every visible event card (artist name, a French-language date string, and a per-event detail link) is already fully rendered as static server-side markup in the plain HTTP response.

probe_history.reason: A plain curl GET of https://le-zenith.com/program immediately exposed 8 fully-rendered `.card-show` event blocks, each with an artist name, a French date string, and a detail-page link. No escalation was required; Level 1 fully answered the investigation question.

venue_reference: Zénith Paris - La Villette — 211 Avenue Jean Jaurès, 75019 Paris (large concert arena, Parc de la Villette)

identity.notes: The retained page's own <title> reads 'Programme | Zénith Paris - La Villette' at the venue's own domain le-zenith.com, matching the well-known Parc de la Villette arena. Every image asset URL is self-hosted under le-zenith.com/media/cache/.

site_classification.platform: Custom server-rendered CMS (no WordPress/wp-json signal detected). Every card repeats the identical `.card-show` structure directly in the plain HTTP response.

title.notes: Each card's own `.card-show__artist` text, stated directly.

start_date.notes: Each card's own `.card-show__date` text (e.g. 'Samedi 05 sept. 2026'), a French day-name/day/abbreviated-month/year string, stated directly. At least 2 of 8 sampled cards (BINI, 'Annulé'/Cancelled; Hexagone MMA, 'Reporté'/Postponed) show this same date struck through (<del>) with no replacement date printed anywhere on the page — those two are honestly excluded from this source's published Observations (ingestion/zenith-la-villette/observation-adapter.mjs's toObservations()) rather than asserting a struck-through date as still valid, and are never silently dropped from extraction itself (ingestion/zenith-la-villette/discovery.mjs still returns them, flagged 'cancelled: true').

time.notes: No time-of-day is shown anywhere on this list-card view for any sampled event — a calendar date only.

end.notes: No end date/time is shown anywhere on this list-card view.

venue_location.notes: The retained page's own <title> directly states the venue name; this is a single-venue source (every card is this one venue), so every Observation is resolved to it by source_id, not per-record text.

source_record_id.notes: This source exposes no separate machine-readable event id field; each card's own '/shows/{Name}-{numeric-id}' href is this source's own permanent permalink, so the URL-encoded slug (decoded) is used as source_record_id — the same documented judgement already established for tempodrom-berlin-01/badehaus-berlin-01 (a site's own URL-slug permalink as its stable identity). The numeric suffix within the slug (e.g. '22278') looks like it may itself be a stable per-show id, but this was not independently re-verified across repeated fetches within this bounded investigation, so only the full slug (not the bare number alone) is claimed PROVEN here.

event_url.notes: Each card's own href, stated directly, resolved against the venue's own domain.

price.notes: No price of any kind is shown anywhere on this list-card view for any sampled event — this source's own ticketing is entirely delegated to third-party links (Ticketmaster, and a secondary 'P.S.H'/yoolabox listing) that are never resolved to a price on this page itself.

blockers.description: This one plain fetch returned 8 event cards; whether this represents the venue's complete near-term calendar or a bounded/paginated subset was not confirmed within this bounded investigation (no pagination control was observed on the fetched page, but this was not exhaustively verified).

This source shows no machine-readable music/non-music category field on its cards; every sampled card in this investigation was in fact music/live-performance-relevant (including the excluded-for-cancellation Hexagone MMA, which is a combat-sports event, not music) — a production collector should add an explicit category/keyword filter before broad activation, mirroring ingestion/accor-arena/discovery.mjs's own bounded approach, rather than assuming every future card is music.

DETERMINISTIC_DERIVATION offline-proof evidence retained (tests/zenith-la-villette.test.mjs, 5/5 passing), including an explicit test proving the cancelled/struck-through-date card is correctly excluded rather than fabricated as valid.

evidence.description: The venue's official programme page — the full raw response was 103,194 bytes, dominated by navigation/CSS/menu markup carrying no event data. This file retains the page's own <title> plus the FIRST 8 real `.card-show` event listing blocks verbatim (byte-for-byte substring), each with an artist name, a French-language date string, and a per-event detail link. At least one sampled card (BINI) shows its date struck through with no replacement printed nearby — retained here exactly as served, disclosed in this description and honestly reflected in field_assessment.start_date.
evidence.method: curl (plain HTTP GET, descriptive User-Agent, no authentication, no browser); response then truncated to title + the first 8 .card-show blocks, disclosed in this description

evidence.description: A real, dependency-free, no-network offline test suite (tests/zenith-la-villette.test.mjs) re-parsing this investigation's own retained fixture (fixtures/zenith-la-villette-paris/program.html, a copy of ev-cards) via ingestion/zenith-la-villette/discovery.mjs + observation-adapter.mjs and reproducing the exact claimed field values deterministically, including correct exclusion of both struck-through/cancelled cards (5/5 tests passing).
